layout_structure.title_text: Key Insight 1: Diffuse LiDAR improves spatial coverage over sparse LiDAR
layout_structure.layout_description: The slide uses a two-column comparison layout to contrast two types of LiDAR technology. At the top, a bold title is left-aligned and accompanied by a lightbulb icon. The main content is divided into two side-by-side panels: 'Sparse LiDAR' on the left (marked with a pink icon) and 'Diffuse LiDAR' on the right (marked with a green icon). Each panel contains a vertical stack of three visual elements: a 3D diagram showing a sensor scanning a vase, a small line graph of photon counts over time, and a 2D cross-section diagram of a sensor scanning a wavy surface. The 'Sparse LiDAR' side uses thin red lines to represent narrow laser beams, while the 'Diffuse LiDAR' side uses wide green and purple shaded cones to represent diffuse illumination and a wide instantaneous field of view (IFOV). Below each panel, summary text with arrows highlights the trade-offs: the left side shows decreased spatial coverage and decreased depth ambiguity, while the right side shows increased spatial coverage and increased depth ambiguity. The background is clean white with a decorative light blue and purple wave pattern at the bottom.
